message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **OS** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (the official “ubuntu‑2004‑lts” image family) |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard‑8` (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed) |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA Tesla A100 (the closest match to an RTX A6000 that’s currently offered on GCP) |
| **Boot disk** | 50 GB SSD |
| **Zone** | `us‑central1‑b` (pick your own zone) |

> **NOTE**  
> Google Cloud does not offer an exact “RTX A6000” GPU. The closest equivalent is the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** (`nvidia-tesla-a100`). If you specifically need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to wait until GCP adds it or use a different provider.

---

## 1️⃣  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1. Authenticate (if you haven’t already)
gcloud auth login

# 2. Set your project
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project-id"          # <-- replace with your project ID
ZONE="us-central1-b"                     # <-- pick your preferred zone

# 3. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-instance \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: run a script at boot
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Attach a GPU (`type=` + `count=`) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pick the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Size & type of the root disk |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keep the VM running during maintenance |
| `--scopes` | Grant full Cloud Platform access (adjust if you want tighter scopes) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script on first boot |

> **Tip:** If you want to use a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-16`) or a different zone, just change the values above.

---

## 2️⃣  Using the REST API (HTTP)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom script or CI/CD pipeline), here’s a **sample POST request** you can adapt.

### Endpoint

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

Replace `{project}` with your project ID and `{zone}` with your chosen zone.

### Request Body (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to send the request

1. **Get an OAuth 2.0 access token** (you can use `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` or any other method).
2. **Send the request** with an HTTP client (curl, Postman, etc.):

```bash
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/instances"
```

> Replace `@instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON body above.

---

## 3️⃣  Quick Checklist Before Running

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| 1 | **Billing enabled** on your project. |
| 2 | **Compute Engine API** enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`). |
| 3 | **GPU quota** for the selected zone (check via `gcloud compute accelerator-types list`). |
| 4 | **Firewall rules** allowing SSH (port 22) if you plan to connect. |
| 5 | **IAM permissions** (e.g., `roles/compute.admin` or `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`). |

---

## 4️⃣  After Creation

Once the instance is running, you can:

* SSH into it: `gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-instance --zone=${ZONE}`
* Verify the GPU: `nvidia-smi` (should show the A100)
* Install CUDA, cuDNN, or any deep‑learning framework you need.

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-instance \
    --project=my-gcp-project-id \
    --zone=us-central1-b \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd
```

That’s all you need to spin up a powerful Ubuntu 20.04 VM with an NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPU on Google Cloud!
